handoff.goals: Install the appropriate PostHog JavaScript/Node SDK dependencies with the project package manager.
handoff.did: Ran `npm install posthog-node` for future server-side Node route/error instrumentation, then `npm install posthog-js` for the existing browser application. npm resolved real published versions and updated the manifest and lockfile. `package.json` now declares `posthog-js` (`^1.435.6`) and `posthog-node` (`^5.55.0`); `package-lock.json` locks their resolved dependency graph. These packages enable the later browser interaction funnel/events and server-side meaningful-route/error telemetry.
handoff.forNextAgent: Import `posthog-js` in the browser/client integration and `posthog-node` only for server-side tracking. Configuration must use actual environment values, guard missing configuration as required by COMMANDMENTS, and not hardcode token or host.
handoff.evidence: `npm install posthog-node` completed successfully (3 packages added, 0 vulnerabilities). `npm install posthog-js` completed successfully (10 packages added, 0 vulnerabilities). Final manifest and lockfile checks confirm both SDK declarations.

handoff.goals: Initialize PostHog for the Node/Vercel application, configure environment variables through wizard tools, and document the keys for collaborators.
handoff.did: Created `lib/posthog.js` as the shared server-side singleton. It reads `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `POSTHOG_HOST` from `process.env`, constructs `PostHog` from `posthog-node` with `enableExceptionAutocapture: true`, `flushAt: 1`, and `flushInterval: 0`, throws the required clear development error when either setting is absent, and is a production no-op (`posthog` is `null`) if configuration is absent. Created `.env.example` with placeholder values for both keys. Used `set_env_values` to write the supplied real project token and host to the uncommitted `.env`; `check_env_keys` confirmed both are present. This creates the common client later route instrumentation should feed into product analytics and error tracking.
handoff.forNextAgent: Import the named singleton with `import { posthog } from '../lib/posthog.js'` (adjust relative path by route), guard calls with `if (posthog)`, and for each Vercel/serverless handler that captures an event, call `await posthog.flush()` before returning so batched events are delivered. The app is server-side Node/Vercel functions only for this integration; no browser client or CSP was added. No CSP was found in project application/deployment files, so no `script-src`, `connect-src`, or `worker-src` directive was touched. `package.json` now declares `posthog-node` version `^5.55.0` (observed during verification).
handoff.evidence: Read back `lib/posthog.js` and `.env.example`; `check_env_keys` reported both POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN and POSTHOG_HOST present in `.env` and documented by `.env.example`. No builds, linters, or tests were run as directed.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed `NODE_ENV` or `VERCEL_ENV` is set to `production` in production deployments; otherwise missing analytics configuration deliberately fails loudly outside production.

handoff.goals: Wire PostHog user identification using a stable application user identifier at the appropriate client or request boundary.
handoff.did: No files were changed. The app is server-side Node/Vercel, but its customer order endpoint is unauthenticated and only receives order/contact data. Dashboard access uses one shared password and a signed session cookie that encodes expiry/signature only, not an operator identity. Therefore there is no stable per-user primary key, UUID, or account identifier to pass as a PostHog distinct ID; using order IDs, email/name, phone, or the shared dashboard credential would violate the identity requirements and/or create incorrect person attribution.
handoff.forNextAgent: Do not add identify calls or fabricate distinct IDs. Existing and later server-side captures should remain anonymous unless the app introduces authenticated user/operator accounts with a stable user ID. If that happens, bind that ID once per authenticated request (and use any email/name only as person properties).
handoff.evidence: Read `api/orders.js`, `api/dashboard/login.js`, `api/dashboard/logout.js`, `lib/dashboard-session.js`, and dashboard API handlers. `api/orders.js` accepts unauthenticated order details and only receives a generated order ID after persistence; dashboard sessions contain a timestamp/HMAC based on one shared password, with no user record or ID.
handoff.assumptions: The visible API handlers and dashboard-session implementation represent all identity/authentication mechanisms in this application.

handoff.goals: Ensure uncaught application errors reach PostHog through the supported Node SDK mechanism, configured centrally without per-route manual exception capture.
handoff.did: No files were edited. The prior initialization step already configures the shared posthog-node singleton in lib/posthog.js with enableExceptionAutocapture: true, which is the Node SDK-supported mechanism for uncaught exceptions and unhandled promise rejections. The inspected server bootstrap is a native Node static server (not Express), so no framework-specific error-handler hook is required; the Express-only setupExpressErrorHandler integration does not apply. This preserves centralized exception telemetry and avoids adding scattered manual capture calls.
handoff.forNextAgent: Error tracking is centrally enabled through posthog-node exception autocapture in lib/posthog.js. There is no Express application to wire with setupExpressErrorHandler. No dependency installation, builds, tests, or lint commands were run.
handoff.evidence: Read the Node error-tracking reference, framework commandments, lib/posthog.js, and server.js. lib/posthog.js constructs PostHog with enableExceptionAutocapture: true; server.js uses node:http rather than Express.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the API functions are deployed as independent Node/Vercel handlers, so the Node SDK's uncaught exception/unhandled rejection hooks apply and no shared framework error middleware exists.

handoff.goals: Select meaningful business actions, instrument their real server-side success paths with PostHog capture calls, and record the event contract.
handoff.did: Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json` with nine core events: customer order creation; successful dashboard sign-in and sign-out; dashboard order update/delete; payment verification completion; and tracking record create/delete/manual sync. Added guarded `posthog.capture()` calls after each corresponding successful action in the serverless handlers, followed by `await posthog.flush()` before responding. Event properties are restricted to operational categories and aggregate counts (for example service, quantity, payment method, updated field names, carrier, and verification counts); no order IDs, tracking codes, addresses, contact data, names, or other PII are captured. All captures are intentionally personless because the prior identity handoff established that this app has no stable user/operator identifier.
handoff.forNextAgent: Review the six edited handlers and the JSON event plan. The event captures use the existing named singleton from `lib/posthog.js`, are guarded when configuration is unavailable, and flush in each short-lived Vercel handler. There is no identity gap to resolve: all events are anonymous by design because this unauthenticated/customer and shared-password dashboard application has no stable distinct ID.
handoff.evidence: Read back every edited handler and the event-plan JSON. Confirmed captures occur only after successful mutations/actions, use snake_case event names, avoid PII, and await flush. Corrected payment verification properties after inspecting `lib/payment-verification.js`, which returns numeric counters rather than arrays. No builds, linters, or tests were run as directed.
handoff.assumptions: A capture without a distinct ID is supported by the configured posthog-node SDK and is the intended personless behavior required by the identity handoff.

handoff.did: Created the PostHog dashboard `Analytics basics (wizard)` and attached five wizard-tagged insights: `Customer orders created (wizard)` (daily order_created trend), `Orders by payment method (wizard)` (order_created segmented by payment_method), `Payment verification completions (wizard)` (daily payment_verification_completed trend), `Tracking record operations (wizard)` (daily create/delete/manual-sync series), and `Dashboard order management activity (wizard)` (daily update/delete series). These tiles form an operational starter dashboard; the expected downstream views are order volume and payment mix, payment verification activity, tracking workflow activity, and dashboard order-maintenance activity. handoff.forNextAgent: Dashboard is ready at https://us.posthog.com/project/640025/dashboard/2158695. It has five attached saved insights and will populate automatically after the deployed handlers emit their instrumented events. No code or project files were edited in this task.
handoff.evidence: PostHog MCP returned dashboard id 2158695 and confirmed one tile attachment per created insight. `insight-query` executed for all five saved insights; four returned 30 daily zero-value rows and the payment-method breakdown returned no data for the period.
handoff.assumptions: The event names and payment_method event property used in the insight definitions match the capture-step handoff: order_created, payment_verification_completed, tracking_record_created, tracking_record_deleted, tracking_record_manual_sync, dashboard_order_updated, and dashboard_order_deleted.

handoff.goals: Configure PostHog log capture for the supported Node/Vercel runtime using the documented OTLP approach, while exporting only purpose-written log lines added by this integration.
handoff.did: Installed and read the `logs-nodejs` skill and its Node OTLP reference. Added `lib/posthog-logs.js`, which conditionally configures a dedicated OpenTelemetry `dukedrop.posthog` logger with a `NodeSDK`, `BatchLogRecordProcessor`, and PostHog OTLP HTTP exporter. It derives the logs endpoint from `POSTHOG_HOST`, authenticates from `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`, preserves the project’s development missing-configuration error/production no-op convention, and force-flushes per short-lived request. It does not connect the exporter to console, root, or existing application loggers. Added four safe, structured INFO log calls only after successful operations: order creation, dashboard order update, payment verification completion, and tracking sync completion. Their attributes contain only service/quantity, allowlisted update-field names, and aggregate counts—no request bodies, identifiers, or customer/operator data.
handoff.forNextAgent: Review must install these packages by name (do not add versions): `@opentelemetry/sdk-node`, `@opentelemetry/exporter-logs-otlp-http`, `@opentelemetry/api-logs`, `@opentelemetry/resources`, and `@opentelemetry/sdk-logs`. The configured environment variable names are `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `POSTHOG_HOST`; both are present in the real `.env` and documented in `.env.example`. Delivery is unverified until deployed and observed. To test, complete an otherwise valid customer order through `POST /api/orders`; it emits `order created`, which should appear in PostHog Logs at https://us.posthog.com/logs. The dashboard order PATCH, payment verification POST, and tracking sync POST success paths emit the other three lines. Only log records created by this run’s `dukedrop.posthog` logger are exported. If broader export is wanted later, explicitly emit app logger records through this dedicated logger/exporter; do not attach the exporter to existing/root loggers without a separate privacy and volume review.
handoff.evidence: Read the framework commandments, Node log skill, and Node OTLP reference before implementation. Inspected the existing runtime/logging setup and found no OpenTelemetry files or existing PostHog log export. Read back all five changed files after editing; each configured success path emits and awaits `flushPosthogLogs()`. `check_env_keys` confirmed both required configuration keys are present.
handoff.assumptions: No OpenTelemetry dependency/version or tracing provider was present before this task, based on the repository inspection and upstream handoffs. No dependency installation, manifest/lockfile change, build, lint, or runtime delivery test was performed because this task explicitly leaves those for review.
